title: What Happens If You Jump Into Jupiter? #Shorts
script: If you jumped into Jupiter wearing a spacesuit, you would not land on a surface. Jupiter is a gas giant with no solid ground. You would free-fall through freezing ammonia clouds at over one hundred thousand miles per hour. Within minutes, the atmospheric pressure would equal being buried under thousands of miles of ocean, crushing you instantly before reaching molten diamond rain. title: The Heaviest Teaspoon in the Universe #Shorts
script: A single teaspoon of a neutron star weighs over six billion tons. That is heavier than all of Mount Everest combined. When a massive star runs out of nuclear fuel, its core collapses with such immense force that protons and electrons are crushed into pure neutrons. A single sugar-cube sized chunk dropped on Earth would slice straight through our planet like a laser. Subscribe to SciBytes for more mind-bending science!

title: What Happens If the Sun Vanishes Right Now? #Shorts
script: If the Sun vanished right now, you would not notice for eight minutes and twenty seconds. Gravity travels at the speed of light, meaning Earth would continue orbiting empty space in broad daylight. But at the eight minute mark, sudden pitch black darkness would engulf the globe. Without solar gravity, Earth would violently slingshot into deep space at sixty-seven thousand miles per hour into absolute zero. Subscribe to SciBytes for daily mind-bending physics!

title: What Happens Inside a Black Hole? #Shorts
script: As you cross the event horizon of a black hole, the gravitational pull on your feet becomes millions of times stronger than on your head. This extreme tidal force stretches your entire body into a thin strand of atoms in a process physicists call spaghettification. From outside, an observer would see you freeze at the edge forever, but for you, time rushes toward the infinite singularity. Subscribe to SciBytes for more mind-bending physics!

title: Why Does Earth Glow From Space? #Shorts
script: When astronauts look at Earth from the International Space Station, they witness an eerie neon aura called airglow. This is not the northern lights. During the day, ultraviolet radiation energizes oxygen and nitrogen molecules in the upper atmosphere. At night, these energized atoms release that trapped power as a mesmerizing green and gold luminescence floating fifty miles above our cities. Subscribe to SciBytes for daily mind-bending science!

title: What If the Sun Became a Black Hole? #Shorts
sub_header: IF THE SUN WAS A BLACK HOLE
script: If the Sun instantly collapsed into a black hole of the exact same mass, Earth would not get sucked in. Because the gravitational pull remains completely identical, our planet would continue orbiting at the exact same distance. But without solar radiation, global temperatures would plummet to minus one hundred degrees in weeks, freezing the oceans into solid ice. Subscribe to SciBytes for more mind-bending science!

The only reason it does not crash down is because that colossal weight is dispersed into trillions of microscopic droplets suspended on warm updrafts. Subscribe to SciBytes for more crazy physics!

title: Did You Know Time Moves Slower on Your Feet? #Shorts
script: According to Einsteins theory of general relativity, the closer you are to a gravitational mass, the slower time ticks. Because your feet are closer to Earths center of gravity than your head, time moves measurably slower at ground level. Over an entire human lifetime, your feet are literally a tiny fraction of a second younger than your brain. Subscribe to SciBytes for more mind-bending physics!
